Decompose model-conditional predictive variance

Source: R/pb_predict_variance.R
pb_predict_variance.Rd

Separates between-refit variation of conditional means from expected conditional outcome variance according to the law of total variance.

Usage

pb_predict_variance(results, newdata)

Arguments

results

A pb_boot object from pb_simulate() or pb_parallel(), created with keep_fits = TRUE.

newdata

Nonempty data frame of covariates for future observations.

Value

A data frame with prediction, parameter_variance, observation_variance, total_variance, and successful_replicates for each row of newdata.

Details

Supports unweighted Gaussian lm, Poisson glm and MASS::glm.nb. Parameter variance uses the finite-mixture denominator B, not B - 1. No new random draws are made. These are model-conditional estimates rather than guarantees of predictive coverage.

See also

pb_predict_interval(), pb_predict_observations()

Examples

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
boot <- pb_simulate(fit, n = 30, seed = 1, keep_fits = TRUE)
pb_predict_variance(boot, mtcars[1:2, c("wt", "hp")])
#>   prediction parameter_variance observation_variance total_variance
#> 1   23.57233          0.1870949              7.26565       7.452745
#> 2   22.58348          0.1860647              7.26565       7.451714
#>   successful_replicates
#> 1                    30
#> 2                    30
